file_name: Tran-Nguyen K - 2022 - Mobile App Prototype in Older Adults for Postfracture Acute Pain Management User Centered Design App.txt

barriers.description: Testing the medium-fidelity prototype using only a desktop emulator limited the realism of evaluations and may have prevented detection of usability problems present on real mobile devices.
barriers.justification: This testing environment constraint directly hindered the designers' ability to evaluate designs and understand the context of use on target devices, reducing the effectiveness of the Evaluate designs and Understand context of use workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: We used only an emulator on a desktop computer to test our medium-fidelity mHealth prototype; thus, it is possible that some usability problems were not detected.

barriers.description: Conducting workshops and usability tests remotely due to COVID-19 may have altered participant interactions with the prototype and with the research team.
barriers.justification: Remote delivery affected the designer–participant interaction and likely constrained the team's ability to facilitate user involvement and to thoroughly observe and interpret natural use, hindering Manage user understanding and Facilitate user involvement workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: First, our studies were conducted remotely owing to the COVID-19 pandemic restrictions, which may have affected the participants’ interactions with the prototype.

barriers.description: Recruitment required participants to have internet access, a desktop or laptop with camera/microphone, and the usability protocol required use of Zoom, biasing the sample toward higher technological literacy.
barriers.justification: These participation requirements limited who could take part and therefore constrained the designers' ability to engage a representative range of users and to manage a comprehensive understanding of the target population, hindering Manage user understanding, Facilitate user involvement, and Understand context of use.
barriers.reference_excerpt:
Inclusion criteria for the workshop participants were as follows: they must (1) be aged ≥50 years; (2) have sustained at least one skeletal fracture after the age of 40 years; (3) be able to communicate in English; and (4) have access to the internet and own a desktop computer or laptop computer with a camera and microphone.

Third, the protocol for the usability tests required participants to have access to Zoom. Consequently, these participants likely had higher technological literacy than those who would never have used videoconferencing tools.

barriers.description: Convenience sampling (recruiting prior study participants and clinic patients) likely biased the participant pool toward individuals already familiar with osteoporosis and injury management.
barriers.justification: This sampling bias limited designers' ability to elicit broad, representative user requirements and to fully manage user understanding and specify requirements for less-informed users, hindering Manage user understanding and Specify user requirements workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Second, convenience sampling may have biased our results, as we recruited participants who had participated in previous studies on bone health or who had been evaluated in orthopedic clinics at our center. Design workshop participants were well aware of osteoporosis and its negative impacts and may have had prior knowledge related to injury management.
